parole.significato: beam (large piece of timber or iron)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish balka, with an unexpected shift of a > e first occurring in the 16th century. Compare Kashubian balka and Slovincian balka. Doublet of balkon.

parole.significato: feature, quality, trait
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish cecha (“token, stamp”). Doublet of cych and token.

parole.significato: duvet cover; pillowcase
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish cecha (“cover”).

parole.significato: brick (hardened rectangular block of mud, clay, etc., used for building)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish cegła.

parole.significato: three (three dots on a die; triangle)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish dryja. Doublet of trzy.

parole.significato: fencing
parole.testo: From German fechten + -unek, from Middle High German vëhten, from Old High German fehtan, from Proto-West Germanic *fehtan, from Proto-Germanic *fehtaną, from Proto-Indo-European *peḱ-.

parole.significato: cigarette holder
parole.testo: From German Pfeife + -ka, from Middle High German pfīfe, from Old High German pfīfa, from Proto-West Germanic *pīpā, from Vulgar Latin *pipa, from Latin pipō.

parole.significato: estate exchange (in the former Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, a barter or an exchange of noble estates for royal lands…
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish frymark, borrowed from Middle High German vrimarket, from vri + market.

parole.significato: to gush, to pour forth, to spout
parole.testo: From German gießen + -ać, from Middle High German giezen, from Old High German giozan, from Proto-West Germanic *geutan, from Proto-Germanic *geutaną, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰewd- (“to pour”).

parole.significato: edifice (building; structure; architectural fabric, especially a large and spectacular one)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish gmach, borrowed from Middle High German gemach, from Old High German gimah, from Proto-West Germanic *gamak.

parole.significato: populace, rabble
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish gmin, borrowed from Middle High German gemein, from Old High German gimeini, from Proto-West Germanic *gamainī. Doublet of gmina.

parole.significato: rape (act of forcibly having sex with someone)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German gewalt, from Old High German giwalt, from Proto-West Germanic *gawald, from Proto-Germanic *gawaldą. See German Gewalt.

parole.significato: harp (a musical instrument consisting of a body and a curved neck, strung with strings of varying length that are strok…
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish arfa.

parole.significato: queen (chess piece)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish hetman, borrowed from Middle High German houbetman / heuptman, from Old High German houbitman. The e in hetman attests to a borrowing from an East Central German dialect, in which Middle High German -öu- gives -ē-.

parole.significato: blanket (heavy, loosely woven fabric, usually large and woollen, used for warmth while sleeping or resting)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German kotze, from Old High German chozzo, from Proto-West Germanic *kottō, from Proto-Germanic *kuttô. Cognate with Slovene koconog (see koconoga kanja).

parole.significato: form, shape (appearance of something in terms of its arrangement in space, especially its outline)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish kstałt. Doublet of gestalt (“gestalt”).

parole.significato: lovage (Levisticum officinale)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish lubszczek, from Middle High German lübestecke, from Old High German lubistechal, from Proto-West Germanic *lubistik, from Latin lubisticum, libisticum, from ligusticum, from Ancient Greek λῐγῠστῐκόν (lĭgŭstĭkón), from Ancient Greek Λῐγῠστῐκός (Lĭgŭstĭkós), from Ancient Gree

parole.significato: land, landmass (area of the Earth not covered by water)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish ląd, land, borrowed from Middle High German in the 14th century. The original etymon is probably lende (“landing place”), from Old High German lentī (cf. regional German Lände), rather than lant (“land”), though the latter has influenced the sense. Both eventually derived f

parole.significato: mint (money-producing building or institution)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish minca, mińca, from Middle High German, from Old High German muniz, munizza, from Proto-West Germanic *munit, from Latin monēta. Doublet of manat and moneta (“coin”).

parole.significato: wall (defensive rampart)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish mur, borrowed from Middle High German mūr, from Old High German mūra.

parole.significato: stake (piece of wood)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German pfāl, from Old High German pfāl.

parole.significato: parsnip (the plant Pastinaca sativa)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German pasternack, pasternacke, from Old High German pestinac, from Proto-West Germanic *pastinakā, from Latin pastināca.

parole.significato: frame (connected strips surrounding a mirror, picture or glass)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish rama.

parole.significato: market, marketplace (city square or other fairly spacious site where traders set up stalls and buyers browse the mercha…
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish rynek. Doublet of ranga, ring, krąg, and kręg.

parole.significato: ridge (narrow strip of soil cut off and laid down by a plough)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German scība, from Old High German skība, from Proto-West Germanic *skībā. Doublet of szajba, szyb, and szyba.

parole.significato: grease, lubricant (substance used to reduce friction)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German smër, from Old High German smero, from Proto-West Germanic *smeru, from Proto-Germanic *smerwą, from Proto-Indo-European *smérus.

parole.significato: head man (elected head of a rural subdivision, usually a village, or part of a large village known as a sołectwo)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish sołtes, szałtys, szołtys, szołtysz, from Middle High German schultheize (whence also German Schultheiß), from Old High German sculdheizo, from Proto-West Germanic *skuldihaitijō.

parole.significato: granary (storage facility)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German spīcher, from Old High German spīhhāri, from Proto-West Germanic *spīkārī, from Late Latin spīcārium, with an unexplained epenthetic “-l-”. Compare German Speicher. Doublet of spichrz.

parole.significato: granary (storage facility)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German spīcher, from Old High German spīhhāri, from Proto-West Germanic *spīkārī, from Late Latin spīcārium. Compare German Speicher. Doublet of spichlerz.

parole.significato: to use, to apply, to employ [with w (+ locative) ‘at what’]
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish stosować.

parole.significato: line, streak
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish strych, from Middle High German strich, from Old High German strih, from Proto-West Germanic *striki, from Proto-Germanic *strikiz, from Proto-Indo-European *strig-ís, from the root *streyg- (“to stroke”).

parole.significato: to injure pasterns by catching one leg with the other
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish strychować, from Middle High German strīchen, from Old High German strīhhan, from Proto-West Germanic *strīkan.

parole.significato: school (educational institution)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish szkoła. Doublet of schola.

parole.significato: art (conscious production or arrangement of sounds, colours, forms, movements, or other elements in a manner that affec…
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish sztuka. Sense 1 was derived from sense 12. Doublet of stiuk.

parole.significato: attack, assault, onslaught
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish sturm, szturm, from Middle High German sturm, from Old High German sturm, from Proto-West Germanic *sturm, from Proto-Germanic *sturmaz, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)twerH-. Doublet of sztorm.

parole.significato: newt (amphibian)
parole.testo: Perhaps from trach + -ka, from Middle High German trache, tracke, drache, dracke, from Old High German trahho, from Proto-West Germanic *drakō, from Latin dracō, from Ancient Greek δράκων (drákōn). Doublet of Drakula.

parole.significato: scale (device to measure mass or weight)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish waga.

parole.significato: watch, guard duty
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German warte, from Old High German warta, from Proto-West Germanic *wardu.

parole.significato: compensation (something which is regarded as an equivalent; something which compensates for loss)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish wet.

parole.significato: lye (alkaline solution)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German louge, from Old High German louga, from Proto-West Germanic *laugu, from Proto-Germanic *laugō.

parole.significato: żur (sour rye soup)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German sūr. Doublet of ser.
